SCENE 2  THE BEACH: SEE WHAT HAPPENED FIRST

SCENE 5  CARE STATION: STABILIZE BEFORE CLEANING

SCENE 8  THE ARCHIVE: CARE FRAGMENT AND FINAL REVIEW
Safety Boundary
Record Reliability
Care and Patience
Recovery Evidence
ARCHIVIST
TOURIST
MARINA / RESCUE HOTLINE
An emblem missing all four corners hangs above a glass display. Amber light glows in the first empty space as waves and brief bird calls sound in the distance.

The first fragment is not about holding a living creature in your arms. It is about knowing when to step back.

You will enter a fictional rescue process. Historical facts and creative material will be identified separately. Your task is to observe, establish a boundary, make contact, keep records, and wait for professional judgment.

Near the tide line, a black-and-white seabird lies beside the rocks. Some of its feathers are matted into dark clumps, and its body still moves faintly. Two tourists are approaching while an unleashed dog barks at it.

Record only visible facts from a safe distance. The species, body temperature, degree of hunger, cause of injury, and source of contamination remain unverified.

TOURIST: Shouldn't we just carry it back into the water? It looks cold.

The system will not erase unsafe handling. How you approach will change order at the site and leave traceable consequences at the professional handoff.

TOURIST: It must be freezing, and it has probably been starving for days.

The system requires separate fields for direct observation, reports from others, and unverified information. The incident title will shape how later responders understand this record.

Label the source of every item. It is acceptable to record “unknown”; do not turn an assumption into a fact. Dispatch has accepted the case, and the record will be reviewed during the professional handoff.

The rescue vehicle arrives. Marina and the team put on protective equipment, review the boundary and incident card, and approach from the least disruptive direction.

MARINA: Who found the animal first? Has anyone touched it, fed it, washed it, or pushed it back into the water? Did you see that yourself, or did someone else assume it?

Transfer the complete site record: discovery time, boundary setup, agency contact, changes at the scene, and every item that remains uncertain. Original attachments and source labels should accompany the handoff.

The player supports logistics from behind an observation window. The status board shows low strength, elevated stress, and heavy feather contamination.

MARINA: Cleaning is one part of a professional process; faster is not always better. The animal must first be admitted, clinically assessed, and stabilized, or the care itself may add strain. The player interface will not show medications, doses, cleaning agents, concentrations, or temperatures.

People on social media demand to know why the animal is not being washed immediately. Managing information, resources, and waiting is also part of care. Professional rescue cannot be reduced to housework or a public performance.

Several days pass in montage. Three recovery records signed by professionals show:
R1: Contamination remains; strength is low; waterproofing has not been assessed.
R2: Appearance and strength have improved; waterproofing is partly restored.
R3: No visible oil remains; strength is stable; waterproofing and swimming performance pass professional checks.

A better appearance cannot replace professional assessment.

Before requesting release, the player must decide what evidence the report will rely on. Keep anthropomorphic claims such as “it looks happy” or “it must miss home” out of the report. Conclusions should rely on multi-day records, functional checks, and professional sign-off.

The professional team completes the final assessment and selects a site with no known contamination that meets the release requirements. The player remains outside the marked line, checking the record and the public viewing distance.

The penguin pauses, then walks into the surf. It does not look back or wave a flipper, and no one runs after it for an embrace.

MARINA: We have completed the part we can be responsible for today. Release gives it a chance to live on its own again; it does not mean we can guarantee what happens next.

The view returns to the Undersea Archive. Within the amber fragment appears a penguin surrounded by a boundary that leaves it space.

Care is not possession, and it is not proof that you saved someone. It means letting the right people take over and remaining responsible through the time when no change can be seen.
